stories.title: Fortune 500 Company Signs Sugar Land Office Lease
stories.excerpt: Primoris Services, a Fortune 500 provider of critical infrastructure services Sugar has signed a 25,352-square-foot office lease at Sugar Land Town Square. The announcement comes as Sugar Land Town Square undergoes a significant redevelopment initiative designed to elevate the tenant experience and further strengthen the district’s appeal to corporate employers, supporting continued economic growth in Sugar Land and the Greater Houston region. Primoris will occupy the 8th floor of 2150 Town Square Place and is expected to begin occupancy in 2027. Primoris was self-represented in lease negotiations, while the landlord was represented by CBRE’s Bubba Harkins, Jenny Sealy and Joel Douthit. Primoris is a provider of infrastructure services to the utility, energy and renewables markets, offering engineering, construction and maintenance services across the utility, energy and renewable infrastructure sectors. Primoris joins a diverse roster of office tenants, including CVR Energy, Industrial Info Resources and Nexus Water Group. In 2025, the City of Sugar Land approved a $12.5 million reinvestment in Sugar Land Town Square to enhance the property and further elevate the tenant experience. The post Fortune 500 Company Signs Sugar Land Office Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Primoris (Fortune 500, infrastructure services) leases 25,352 SF at Sugar Land Town Square, occupancy 2027
Sugar Land Town Square undergoing $12.5M reinvestment; City approved in 2025 to attract corporate tenants
Houston metro office absorption signals demand; Primoris joins CVR Energy, Industrial Info, Nexus Water Group
stories.summary: Primoris Services, a Fortune 500 infrastructure firm, signed a 25,352-square-foot lease on the 8th floor of 2150 Town Square Place in Sugar Land, Texas, with occupancy expected in 2027. The lease arrives as Sugar Land Town Square undergoes a $12.5 million city-backed reinvestment to elevate the tenant experience and competitive positioning. Primoris joins a diversifying roster of corporate tenants including CVR Energy and Industrial Info Resources, signaling sustained office demand in the submarket.
stories.impact: Sugar Land's $12.5M public reinvestment and corporate tenant clustering (Primoris, CVR Energy) suggest sustained job growth and anchor-tenant stability in this outer Houston submarket. This signals steady employment base and worker population retention, supporting multifamily demand in surrounding submarkets; developers should monitor Sugar Land's office velocity and wage profiles for residential absorption tailwinds.

stories.title: HBK CPAs & Consultants Relocates Baltimore Offices to Hunt Valley Complex
stories.excerpt: HBK CPAs & Consultants has signed a lease with Hill Management Services, Inc. for 7,168 square feet of space and recently relocated its Baltimore regional office, together with 15 employees, to the Executive Plaza complex in Hunt Valley, Maryland. Danielle Bridge of Hill Management Services represented the landlord, and Clare Berrang of Singer Demareck Real Estate handled negotiations on behalf of the tenant. The Youngstown, Ohio-based accounting firm entered the Baltimore market following the company’s acquisition of the 30-person McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond late last year.Located at 11350 McCormick Road, the business complex consists of four office towers comprising 550,000 square feet of commercial office space. “Executive Plaza’s positioning within a robust and diverse business community, which provides the perfect environment to service existing customers as well as opportunities to generate new clients, makes the complex ideal for professional services firms such as HBK,” said Beyrodt. The post HBK CPAs & Consultants Relocates Baltimore Offices to Hunt Valley Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HBK CPAs relocated Baltimore regional office to Hunt Valley; 15 employees, 7,168 SF lease signed
HBK entered Baltimore market via 30-person acquisition of McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond late 2024

stories.summary: HBK CPAs & Consultants, a Youngstown-based accounting firm, relocated its Baltimore regional office and 15 employees to a 7,168-square-foot space at Executive Plaza in Hunt Valley, Maryland. The move followed HBK's acquisition of McLean, Koehler, Sparks & Hammond (30 people) in late 2024, marking the firm's entry into the Baltimore market. Executive Plaza is a 550,000-square-foot complex comprising four office towers in a diversified business hub.
stories.impact: HBK's Baltimore market entry via acquisition and Hunt Valley positioning signals regional consolidation and professional services clustering, but delivers modest headcount impact (15 employees) relative to multifamily demand catalysts. Monitor: if HBK expands beyond the acquired 30-person base, it could accelerate Hunt Valley office and adjacent residential demand; for now, low signal for multifamily market in Baltimore.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties Acquires, Fully Leases Puget Sound Biomanufacturing Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties, a joint venture between Tishman Speyer and Bellco Capital, has acquired a recently delivered biomanufacturing facility at 215 Shuksan Way in Everett, Washington, just outside of Seattle. The joint venture acquired the 270,000-square-foot property for $78 million from its second life science fund. In tandem with the acquisition, Breakthrough secured a separate 21-year lease for the entire campus with a global biopharma company to create a U.S. manufacturing facility. 215 Shuksan Way offers a full range of capabilities and amenities, from drug manufacturing, quality control labs and warehouse and distribution logistics to administrative office spaces. The acquisition marks Breakthrough’s first investment in the Puget Sound region. 215 Shuksan Way sits approximately 25 miles north of Seattle along the I-5 corridor. The location provides easy connectivity to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, the commercial airport Paine Field, the Port of Everett and railway access that connects the site to major North American freight corridors. Simultaneously, a global biopharma company committed to a 21-year lease for the entire property, establishing a U.S. manufacturing facility. stories.impact: Everett biomanufacturing campus represents major life sciences anchor and long-term tenant stability, signaling sustained job creation and high-wage employment in Puget Sound corridor. Breakthrough's first Puget Sound investment + 21-year biopharma commitment de-risks the Everett submarket and catalyzes secondary and tertiary supply-chain employment (logistics, admin, engineering support). Multifamily developers should pre-position workforce housing (studio to 2-BR product) in Everett/south Snohomish County to capture biotech employee in-migration over the lease term.

stories.title: J.G. Petrucci, BGO Cold Chain Lease Bethlehem Cold Storage Development
stories.excerpt: J.G. Petrucci Company, Inc. and BGO Cold Chain announced that Freshpet has leased the entire 216,000-square-foot cold storage development at 757 Hellertown Road in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. The facility is scheduled for on-time and on-budget completion by the end of the year, and the property was developed through a joint venture between Petrucci and BGO Cold Chain. The facility is Freshpet’s first dedicated cold storage facility, contributing to the effective distribution of its temperature-sensitive products. The location offers excellent proximity to the company’s existing Bethlehem Kitchen and convenient access to I-78 and other major roadways. stories.impact: Freshpet's 216,000 SF cold storage lease and Bethlehem Kitchen cluster signal consolidation of food manufacturing/logistics in the Allentown-Bethlehem submarket, anchoring a mid-sized employment node. However, cold storage and food manufacturing are capital-intensive, lower-headcount operations relative to their footprint. Modest direct multifamily demand signal unless Freshpet materially expands support staff; flag if supply-chain job clustering accelerates in Lehigh Valley.

stories.title: Historic Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett Listed for Sale
stories.excerpt: Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett, Washington, has listed its historic property at 2324 Lombard Avenue for sale. Kidder Mathews Senior Vice President Steve Pelluer and Associate Vice President Zeke Pelluer are representing the congregation. For more than a century, Trinity has been a place of worship, inclusion, and service. Organized in 1904 as St. Paul Lutheran Church, it became Trinity English Lutheran Church in 1914. “Properties with this combination of character, history, flexibility, and community significance rarely become available,” said Steve Pelluer. Designed by Seattle architecture firm Bebb and Gould, the historic sanctuary has served as a worship site for generations. The 13,728-square-foot property includes 9,644 square feet of church space and a 4,084-square-foot administration building. The 0.41-acre property is adjacent to Clark Park and near downtown Everett, Everett High School, and North Middle School. The church portion dates to the early 1920s, with additions completed in 1940 and 1969. The post Historic Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett Listed for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Trinity Lutheran Church in Everett, Washington, has listed its historic 13,728-square-foot property at 2324 Lombard Avenue for sale. The property, organized in 1904 and built primarily in the early 1920s with additions in 1940 and 1969, comprises a 9,644-square-foot church sanctuary (designed by Seattle's Bebb and Gould firm) and a 4,084-square-foot administration building on 0.41 acres. The site is adjacent to Clark Park and near downtown Everett, Everett High School, and North Middle School.
stories.impact: Trinity's sale signals potential land recycling in downtown Everett, a secondary Seattle market historically underdeveloped for multifamily. The 0.41-acre historic property with park adjacency and school proximity presents mixed-use conversion/adaptive-reuse potential; if repositioned as residential (+ ground-floor community/retail), it could seed downtown Everett revitalization. However, historic designations and community sensitivity require entitlement discipline. Monitor: buyer intent and zoning flexibility to assess whether this unlocks broader Everett downtown multifamily pipeline.

stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M

A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. Monitor: financing availability and construction cost trends for this cohort of outer-Brooklyn oceanfront mixed-use starts; rising rates/caps may stall delivery timelines.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said
bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of multifamily investors hold negative 2H 2026 outlook; 52% underperformed in 1H 2026
Capital markets volatility, persistent interest-rate uncertainty, softer property performance cited; 10Y Treasury at 4.7%, 30Y at 5.2%
Investor sentiment: 6 months ago expected volatility fade and accelerating transaction activity; instead, uncertainty persisted
stories.summary: A Berkadia survey of more than 100 multifamily investment principals found that 61 percent characterize their 2H 2026 outlook as negative due to capital markets volatility and uncertainty, while 52 percent reported that assets underperformed first-half expectations. Interest rates have remained elevated, with the 10-Year Treasury at 4.7 percent and the 30-Year Treasury at 5.2 percent (20-year highs). Senior executives attributed the pessimism to persistent rate volatility, softer operating environments, and property performance below prior-year comparables—reversing optimistic sentiment from six months prior.
stories.impact: Widespread negative investor sentiment and elevated long-duration rates (5.2% 30Y) compress multifamily valuations and development underwriting returns. Tightened financing conditions and cap rate elevation slow acquisition and groundbreaks; expect delayed capital deployment into starts and reduced competitive intensity for land. For Trammell Crow: market dislocation may create opportunistic land acquisition windows in stabilized markets, but development feasibility deteriorates unless construction costs moderate or rent growth accelerates materially. Monitor: any 10Y Treasury break below 4.5% and SOFR futures for refinancing signals.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company's (ARTIC) St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort from special servicing with a $263 million refinance loan. Fortress assumed $188 million in existing debt and supplied $70 million in new capital, with the asset valued at $311 million. The 213-room oceanfront property in Bal Harbour, Florida (north of Miami Beach) had declined significantly: 2024 cash flow was approximately 50 percent of 2021 levels, and the prior CMBS lender (Column Financial) required an interest-rate cap replacement that ARTIC could not secure as the loan matured.
stories.impact: Hospitality distress and capital flight signal softening in high-end coastal lodging; however, this is lodging, not multifamily. Relevance: South Florida cap rates and financing spreads are informational for multifamily underwriting in Miami/Bal Harbour premium residential (luxury condos, rentals). If hospitality is stressed in this affluent corridor, it may signal demand weakness among transient/seasonal affluent travelers, reducing ancillary demand for branded residences. Otherwise, limited direct multifamily impact.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquire retail center, Bayside Queens for $23.5M from Levy Properties
213-04 Northern Boulevard: 24,000 SF built, 74,350 SF air rights (98,478 SF total buildable); urgent care + Bebeang Baby Store
Queens experiencing surge in multifamily development; buyers' intent unclear but air rights suggest conversion/upside potential
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners Real Estate acquired a one-story retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, from Levy Properties for $23.5 million. The 24,000-square-foot property currently houses an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. The site carries 74,350 square feet of air rights, totaling 98,478 buildable square feet. The buyers' development plans remain unclear, but the significant air-rights entitlement in a Queens market experiencing multifamily growth suggests conversion potential.
stories.impact: First Pioneer/ABS acquisition of Bayside retail with substantial air rights capitalizes on Queens's multifamily boom and density upzoning. The 74,350 SF air-rights parcel signals owner intent to unlock residential density; Bayside's 7-train access and affordability thesis make this a classic value-creation site for conversion to rental housing. If First Pioneer develops multifamily here, it adds to the outer-Queens supply pipeline; monitor: local market absorption, rent trends in comparable new Bayside product, and financing availability for the conversion thesis.

stories.title: Pinnacle Group Offloads $128M Condominium and Commercial Portfolio in NYC
stories.excerpt: Pinnacle Group has offloaded a $128 million residential and retail condominium portfolio in New York City, less than a year after selling off its rent-stabilized assets. The massive trade, filed in city records this week, spanned 39 transactions across Queens, Brooklyn and Manhattan. It included nearly 750 residential units, as well as dozens of retail condominiums and several parking lots. The Real Deal first reported on the sale. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, share an address with law firm Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever. The transactions were signed by Stuart Berg, chair of the firm’s real estate practice group. A PincusCo report tied the Friar Park entities and Berg to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based property company William Pears Group. The group, through Tremada, has quietly executed bulk residential transactions across New York City over the years with Berg’s law firm, according to PincusCo. Berg, as well as spokespeople for William Pears Group and Tremada, did not respond to requests for comment. Queens-based property management company Bronstein Properties is the managing agent for the portfolio of units, according to a spokesperson for Bronstein. Pinnacle, led by Joel Wiener, made headlines in May 2025 when it placed a portfolio of roughly 5,000 rent-stabilized apartments across New York City into bankruptcy after facing approximately $574.4 million in debt. Summit Properties won the auction for the portfolio in January, paying $451.3 million for the units. The proceeds from Pinnacle’s most recent sale will pay $66 million to lender Axos Capital, TRD reported, citing filings with the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange by Pinnacle’s Israeli subsidiary Zarasai Group. Another $47 million is currently slated to be deposited into the account of Series C bondholders. A spokesperson for Pinnacle Group could not be reached for comment on the sales. The buyer entities, Friar Park JW, are linked via law firm Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever to Tremada Holdings, an affiliate of London-based property company William Pears Group. The portfolio sale follows Pinnacle's divestiture of rent-stabilized assets less than a year prior, signaling a systematic exit from NYC rental housing.
stories.impact: Pinnacle's $128M portfolio exit (750 units) reflects portfolio rationalization and possible yield-seeking by UK capital (William Pears/Tremada). The bulk sale to foreign institutional buyer may indicate: (1) domestic investor caution on NYC regulatory/rent-control risk, (2) opportunistic foreign capital diving into perceived NYC discount, or (3) Pinnacle's capital redeployment. This signals market fragmentation and potential supply-side ownership churn. For multifamily developers: monitor whether Tremada/William Pears holds for long-term cashflow (stabilizing influence) or flips/repositions (competitive pressure). Regulatory risk and lower domestic investor appetite may depress NYC multifamily valuations and cap rates, creating development headwinds.
